pairs.difference: A (gold pan): the key comes from the upper left. The inner wall of the far rim is lit, the near outer wall and underside fall into a deep dark band, and the nuggets have small sharp highlights on their top-left facets. B (oil lamp): the brass font has one broad glossy hot spot at the front centre and the foot is shaded the same on both sides. Light comes from the front and the flame glow, with no clear side plane. Light bias of 0.745 is just above the real range.
pairs.fix: Light the lamp from the upper left: the brass font bright on the left, a clear darker core shadow running down its right side, and the foot's right half in shadow. Remove the centred front hot spot and keep only a small highlight on the upper-left shoulder.

pairs.difference: A (harmonica): the top cover is lit and turns into a darker front face and a dark underside, with a clear light direction. B (fan): the light and dark alternation across the panels comes from the pleats, not from light. The fan has no overall shadow side, no form turn on the ribs or handle, and no cast shadow. Form contrast of 0.213 and light bias of 0.09 are both below the real range.
pairs.fix: Give the fan one light from the upper left: panels on the left brighter, panels on the right a step darker. Add soft shading where each pleat folds, shade the underside of the handle, and add a soft cast shadow below and to the right.

pairs.difference: A (hat): lit from the upper left. The crown turns gently into shadow on the right, and the underside of the brim drops into a dark core under the crown. B (jacket): lit from the front. The front panel and both sleeves are about equally bright, small highlights sit on every pocket edge, and the only dark areas are the cuff openings. There is no side of the body in shadow.
pairs.fix: Light the jacket from the upper left: the left sleeve and left chest bright, the right sleeve and right side of the body a clear step darker with a soft core shadow. Darken the area under the collar and under the sash.

pairs.difference: A (gas pump): the left face is lit and the right side face is clearly darker, the cap has a dark underside, and the hose casts a shadow on the body. Light and shadow sides are well separated. B (buoy): every cylinder tier is lit from the front with a bright centre stripe and symmetric falloff to both edges. The shadow side is shallow, and form contrast of 0.355 is low.
pairs.fix: Light the buoy from the upper left: the left half of each cylinder tier bright, the right half turning into a clearly darker cool shadow. Darken the area under each ledge and add a darker reflection on the water on the right side.

pairs.difference: A (popcorn cart): the awning scallops have dark undersides, the cart body has a lit front and a darker side, and the wheels cast shadows on the tiles. B (saddle on hay): the leather flap, seat and hay bale are all lit evenly from the front. The bale's top and front faces are almost the same value, and the saddle shows no clear core shadow. Light bias of 0.099 is below the real range.
pairs.fix: Put the light at the upper left: the top of the hay bale clearly brighter than its front face, the right end of the bale in shadow, and a soft cast shadow from the saddle across the hay. Add a darker core under the seat's curl and under the horn.

pairs.difference: A (rocking chair): the whole chair is bright and warm. Spindles and rockers have little difference between lit and shadow sides, and the cushion has only a slight darkening underneath. The only strong darks are floor reflections. B (barrel): a clear key from the left, a core shadow down the right side of the barrel, and a dark cast shadow on the ground to the right.
pairs.fix: Light the chair from the upper left: the left side of every spindle and leg lit and the right side clearly darker. Shade under the seat and cushion, and add a soft cast shadow from the chair on the floor to the right.

pairs.difference: A (boots): soft, gentle modelling. The shafts turn smoothly into shadow on the right, and a soft contact shadow sits under the soles. B (sneakers): photographic studio light. A hard-edged cast shadow falls to the left and white soles stand out in high contrast. Shading range of 0.82 is above the real range, and light bias is almost zero.
pairs.fix: Soften the light on the sneakers: replace the hard cast shadow with a soft, short contact shadow under the soles, and model the uppers with a gentle turn from a lit left side to a darker right side, not a flat studio front light.

pairs.difference: A (cactus): the ribs are shaded the same on both sides of the trunk and the arms are front-lit. The turn into shadow is shallow, and form contrast of 0.404 is below the real range. B (duck): the body has a lit upper left and a clear darker core under the wing and belly, the spring is shaded, and a cast shadow falls on the sand.
pairs.fix: Light the cactus from the upper left: the left side of the trunk and each arm bright and the right side clearly darker, with darker valleys between the ribs on the shadow side and a soft contact shadow where the trunk meets the sand.

pairs.difference: A (fountain): all tiers are warm and evenly lit from the front. The basins show only shallow darkening under their lips and the pedestal has no clear shadow side. B (wagon): a strong key from the left, dark shadow under the bed and between the wheels, and the canvas hoops turn into shade.
pairs.fix: Light the fountain from the upper left: the left half of every basin and the pedestal lit, the right half clearly darker, deep shadow under each basin lip, and a cast shadow from the upper tiers onto the water of the lower basin.

pairs.difference: B is the same lighthouse shown as REAL in the lessons. Its stonework has a darker side on the left, the lantern glows warm, and there is dark shadow under the gallery. A (windmill): the tower is lit from the top, and a crisp, even cast shadow and lit grass make the ground plane more uniform than in the real cards.
pairs.fix: Light the windmill from the side: one side of the wooden legs clearly in cool shadow, a darker side face on the stone base, and a softer, shorter cast shadow.

pairs.difference: A (campfire): the fire lights everything evenly. The stones all have the same warm lit tops, the kettle is bright almost all the way round, and the moonlit side gets no cool fill. Light bias of 0.76 is above the real range. B (binocular viewer): a firm key from the upper left, the right side of the head and the post in clear shadow, and strong form contrast.
pairs.fix: Make the fire light fall off with distance: stones nearest the flames bright orange, far sides of stones and the right side of the kettle dropping into dark cool blue shadow. Add a thin cool moonlight rim on the far edges only.

pairs.difference: A (neck pillow): the tube turns smoothly from a lit top into a dark core under the inner curve, and the pleats are shaded. B (water bottle): the plastic body is flat and washed out with almost no turn from lit side to shadow side, and the cap is barely modelled. Shading range of 0.459 is below the real range.
pairs.fix: Model the bottle as a solid form lit from the upper left: the left side bright with one soft vertical sheen, the right side turning to a clearly darker blue core shadow, and shading under the cap's rim and the loop.

pattern: Generated cards are lit from the front and evenly. Both sides of a form get nearly the same light, the shadow side is shallow, the core shadow is weak, and there are few dark undersides under ledges and rims. Real cards commit to one key from the upper left with a clearly darker cool-tinted side plane. Generated cards also tend to go to extremes: either hard photographic cast shadows or almost no cast and contact shadow.
